newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hogs seen steady-up $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hogs seen steady-up $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct hog prices Wednesday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt higher, supported by outlooks for tighter hog supplies, livestock dealers said.
Hog marketings were heavy on Monday and Tuesday as producers sold hogs held back by harsh wintry-like weather last week in the western Corn Belt, they said.
Now that producers reportedly were through selling the bulk of held-back hogs, marketings were seen light.
Marketings also were seen getting tighter into next week as spring fieldwork advances, sources noted.

The interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog run Monday totaled 121,000 head, USDA said, well over its estimate of 110,000. Tuesday's Iowa/so. Minnesota run was estimated at 110,000 head versus 108,000 a week ago and 106,000 a year ago.
Top prices for hogs delivered to interior Iowa and southern Minnesota plants were seen ranging from $52.50 to $54.00 and Illinois top prices could range $53.50 to $54.00, sources in those areas said.
Indiana/Ohio top hog prices at plants could range $53.00 to $53.50, the dealers said.
